title: analysis.score_docs params and result
description: The deterministic tail of the TEAM ANALYSIS documentation pipeline as one pure function: per-page clarity/usefulness/disclosure scoring (_analyse_page_asset over every cache-miss body), aggregation into the DocQualitySignal (_aggregate_doc_assets), findings (_doc_findings), the action plan (_prioritize_doc_actions), the summary blob, and the coaching insights (_fallback_doc_quality_insights — deterministic; the docs path has no LLM anywhere, which is why one method serves the whole tail). Pure by contract: no DB, no network, no clock; Python reads every page body and sends it as params, writes the score cache from the returned assets afterwards, and gates the insights on real coverage. Page bodies cross the wire but never appear in the result — the sidecar returns only derived assets, mirroring the cache's never-store-bodies rule. Reference implementation: src/yeaboi/analysis/aggregate.py::score_docs (build_score_docs_inputs builds the params). Result key order is contractual — these objects feed json.dumps downstream (contract_version, assets, signal, summary, findings, action_plan, insights).

page.description: One collected doc page, sent VERBATIM: either it carries a version-matched cached 'asset' object (passed through unscored, its own key order preserved) or a 'text' body plus metadata (title, platform, url, key, container, version/timestamp). A page with neither a cached asset nor a non-blank body produces no asset. The result's assets array aligns one-to-one, in order, with the pages that pass that filter — the caller zips them to write the score cache, so a count mismatch is a malformed result.

assets.description: One derived asset per scoreable page, in page order (key order for freshly scored assets: title, platform, clarity, usefulness, owned, actionable, structured, has_code_blocks, marked, url, key, container, version). Never contains page bodies.

signal.description: The DocQualitySignal wire form, keys in dataclass declaration order: pages_scanned, platforms_scanned, avg_clarity, avg_usefulness, clear_pages, mixed_pages, unclear_pages, owned_pages, actionable_pages, structured_pages, avg_ai_likelihood, likely_ai_pages, ai_marked_pages, per_platform, flagged_pages, is_ai_estimate. The two legacy fields are always zero here (kept so old saved profiles round-trip).

summary.description: The blob's summary sub-dict (key order as in the reference: pages_scanned … is_ai_estimate, then small_sample last). small_sample is true below the 5-page trend threshold.

findings.description: _doc_findings' dicts verbatim (base key order link, affected_scope, owner_role, confidence, then the finding fields).

insights.description: Deterministic coaching (start/stop/keep/try; items are {title, detail, evidence[, link]}). Always computed by the seam; the CALLER decides whether the blob earns them (pages were read and coverage did not fail) — that gate is impure state the sidecar never sees.
